text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange members on Thursday elected 12 members to serve on the CME's board of directors, including the exchange's chairman, Jack Sandner.
Sandner has one more year on his term as chairman, but needed to be re-elected to the board to serve it. Sandner was first elected to the CME board in 1977.
The 12 directors on the 34-person board were elected by members on Thursday to represent the three divisions of the exchange.
Directors serve two-year terms. The officers of the board will be elected by the directors on Wednesday, January 22.
Six were elected to represent the full CME division, four from the International Monetary Market (IMM), and two from the Index and Options Market (IOM).

The six CME directors elected were Terrence Duffy, floor broker and trader; Robert Haworth, floor trader; Irwin Rosen, floor broker and trader; William Salatich, floor broker and trader; Joel Stender, a trader, and Sandner.

IMM directors elected were Yra Harris, a floor trader; James Oliff, a floor broker and trader; William Shepard, of Shepard International and David Silverman, floor trader and president of M&S Partner, Ltd.
And the two IOM directors elected were Michael Dowd, senior vice president at First Options of Chicago, Inc and Gary Katler, senior vice president at ING Securities.
